questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-2+4\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-2-4\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-2-4\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{-2+4\text{i}} & =\frac{5}{-2+4\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-2-4\text{i}}{-2-4\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-10-20\text{i}}{4+8\text{i}-8\text{i}-16{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-10-20\text{i}}{4-16{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-10-20\text{i}}{4-16(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-10-20\text{i}}{4+16} \\  & =\frac{-10-20\text{i}}{20}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-10-20\text{i}}{20}=-\frac{10}{20}-\frac{20}{20}\text{i}=-\frac{1}{2}-\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing an Imaginary Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $2+\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $2-\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $2-\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{5\text{i}}{2+\text{i}} & =\frac{5\text{i}}{2+\text{i}}\cdot \frac{2-\text{i}}{2-\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{10\text{i}-5{\text{i}}^{2}}{{2}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{10\text{i}-5(-1)}{4-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{10\text{i}+5}{4+1} \\  & =\frac{5+10\text{i}}{5}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{5+10\text{i}}{5}=\frac{5}{5}+\frac{10}{5}\text{i}=1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Complex Number by an Imaginary Number
questions.problem: If ${z}_{1}=-2-7\text{i}$ and ${z}_{2}=6\text{i}$, then ${z}_{1}$ divided by ${z}_{2}$ equals
questions.worked_solution:
First, we set up the fraction:

$$
\frac{-2-7\text{i}}{6\text{i}}
$$

The denominator is the imaginary number $6\text{i}.$ Note that this can be written as $0+6\text{i},$ so the conjugate is $0-6\text{i},$ or simply $-6\text{i}.$

So, we multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-6\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}_{1}}{{z}_{2}} & =\frac{-2-7\text{i}}{6\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-2-7\text{i}}{6\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-6\text{i}}{-6\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{12\text{i}+42{\text{i}}^{2}}{-36{\text{i}}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{12\text{i}+42(-1)}{-36(-1)} \\  & =\frac{-42+12\text{i}}{36}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-42+12\text{i}}{36}=-\frac{42}{36}+\frac{12}{36}\text{i}=-\frac{7}{6}+\frac{1}{3}\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing an Imaginary Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-2-3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-2+3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-2+3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\text{i}}{-2-3\text{i}} & =\frac{4\text{i}}{-2-3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-2+3\text{i}}{-2+3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{-8\text{i}+12{\text{i}}^{2}}{(-2)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-8\text{i}+12(-1)}{4-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{-12-8\text{i}}{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\frac{-12-8\text{i}}{13}=(-\frac{12}{13})+(-\frac{8}{13})\,\text{i}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Dividing a Real Number by a Complex Number
questions.worked_solution:
The denominator is $-4+3\text{i}$ and its conjugate is $-4-3\text{i}.$ We multiply both the numerator and the denominator by $-4-3\text{i},$ so that the denominator turns into a real number:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{-4+3\text{i}} & =\frac{12}{-4+3\text{i}}\cdot \frac{-4-3\text{i}}{-4-3\text{i}} \\  & =\frac{12(-4-3\text{i})}{(-4)^{2}-(3\text{i})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-48-36\text{i}}{16-(-9)} \\  & =\frac{-48-36\text{i}}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the denominator is a real number, we can write the complex number in the form $a+b\text{i}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{-48-36\text{i}}{25}=(-\frac{48}{25})+(-\frac{36}{25})\,\text{i}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
